name: Zoom
tagline: Build a Zoom General app and plug it into Composio. Works in your own account at once; other accounts need Zoom's review.

approvalWait.asStated: Zoom's docs give no review timeline. Zoom staff on devForum: 72-hour SLA excluding weekends; security review can take up to 2 weeks.

cost.asStated: No fee to build, review or publish in any Zoom doc we read. You need a Zoom account with developer access.

steps.title: Set up your Composio account
steps.when: Skip if you already have a Composio project and API key.
instructions: Sign up from the Composio login page.
Open Settings → API keys and copy a key.
Save it as COMPOSIO_API_KEY where your agent runs.
Stay in this project. Auth configs belong to one project.

problems.q: I can't find the API keys page
a: Open the API keys link above after signing in. It opens Settings → API keys for your current project.
If you have several projects, switch to the one you'll use for this agent first.

steps.title: Create a General app
instructions: You must be the Zoom account owner, an admin, or have the Zoom for developers role.
Sign in to marketplace.zoom.us and click Developer in the lower-left pane.
On Created apps, click Develop → Build an app. Select General app, then Create.
On Basic Info, click the pencil to rename the app. Users see this name.
Under Select how the app is managed, pick User-managed unless your agent manages a whole account.
Changing the management type later changes available scopes. Recheck them if you switch.

fields.label: Select how the app is managed
fields.hint: Each user authorizes their own data. Admin-managed: an admin adds it for the whole account

problems.q: I don't see the Developer link
a: It only shows for users with developer permissions.
An admin enables View and Edit for Zoom for developers under User Management → Roles → Role Settings → Advanced features.

steps.title: Set the redirect URL and allow list
instructions: On Basic Info, under OAuth Information, paste the Composio callback into OAuth redirect URL.
Paste the same full URL under OAuth allow lists. Both are required.
Use Strict Mode URL and Subdomain check are optional. Strict mode only allows exact matches.

fields.label: OAuth redirect URL
fields.hint: Must match your Composio auth config exactly

fields.label: OAuth allow lists
fields.hint: Full URL, not just the domain

a: The redirect URL isn't in OAuth allow lists. The OAuth redirect URL field alone isn't enough.
Add the full Composio callback to OAuth allow lists. On a published app, submit an update request.

steps.title: Add granular scopes
instructions: Open Scopes → Add Scopes. Pick a Zoom product, tick scopes, then Done.
Zoom enables no scopes by default. Add only what your tools call.
Fill in Scope Description for each: why your app needs it. Reviewers reject scopes they think you don't need.
Scopes ending in :admin must be authorized by a user with matching admin role permissions.

fields.label: Starter scopes
fields.value: user:read:user meeting:read:meeting meeting:read:list_meetings meeting:write:meeting meeting:update:meeting meeting:delete:meeting cloud_recording:read:list_user_recordings
fields.hint: Granular, user-level. Trim to your tools

warnings.text: Composio's Zoom guide lists classic scopes (meeting:read …). Zoom keeps classic scopes for existing apps; new apps use granular names.

steps.unconfirmed: We couldn't see the Add Scopes picker for a new app, so we didn't confirm classic scopes are hidden there.

problems.q: A tool fails with a scope or permission error
a: Your app lacks the scope that tool's endpoint needs. Look it up in Zoom's granular scopes list.
Add it here and in your Composio auth config, then have the user reconnect. Zoom asks them to authorize again.

steps.title: Copy the development credentials
instructions: On Basic Info, under App Credentials, copy the Client ID and Client secret.
These are development credentials. Production has a different pair, used once you publish.
Store the secret in a secret manager, never in git.

fields.label: Credentials to use now
fields.hint: Switch to Production credentials at go-live

a: The ID or secret is wrong, or you mixed development and production values.
Copy both from the same tab (Development or Production) into your Composio auth config.

steps.title: Create a Composio auth config
instructions: Open the Zoom toolkit in Composio and create an auth config.
Choose OAuth2 and turn on your own developer credentials.
Paste the development Client ID and Client secret.
Replace the pre-filled scopes with the granular scopes you added in Zoom.
Save, then copy the auth config ID (ac_…) for the next step.

fields.label: Redirect URI
fields.hint: Must match the OAuth redirect URL and allow list in Zoom

fields.label: Scopes
fields.value: user:read:user meeting:read:meeting meeting:read:list_meetings meeting:write:meeting meeting:update:meeting meeting:delete:meeting cloud_recording:read:list_user_recordings
fields.hint: Same list as your Zoom app

steps.unconfirmed: We couldn't check how Zoom treats scopes Composio sends that your app lacks. Matching both lists avoids it.

problems.q: The link didn't open the Zoom toolkit
a: Open Auth Configs in the Composio dashboard and click Create Auth Config.
Pick Zoom, choose OAuth2, and turn on your own developer credentials.

steps.title: Use the auth config in your agent
instructions: Pass the auth config ID when you create a session. Your coding agent can paste this in.
Toolkits you don't list keep using Composio's managed auth.

a: The session must include authConfigs with your ac_… ID for zoom.
Toolkits not listed in authConfigs fall back to managed auth.

steps.title: Connect a test account
instructions: Start a connection for a test user and open the link. Sign in with a user in your own Zoom account.
Zoom checks the client ID only after sign-in, so a typo shows up here.
The consent screen should show your app name. Click Allow.
Development apps only work for members of your own Zoom account. Others need the beta or publish steps.
Access tokens last 1 hour; refresh tokens 90 days.
Users already connected through managed auth must reconnect.
steps.unconfirmed: We didn't run a full connection. It needs a Composio API key and a real Zoom sign-in.

problems.q: The consent screen still says Composio
a: The connection used the managed auth config. Pass your ac_… ID in the session.
Existing connections keep their old config. Delete and reconnect them.

problems.q: A user outside my Zoom account can't add the app
a: Unpublished apps only work inside your account.
Request beta sharing for a few testers, or publish the app.

problems.q: A tool fails with Only available for paid users or Webinar plan is missing
a: The user's Zoom plan lacks that feature. Scopes can't fix it.
Use a paid or webinar-enabled test account for those tools.

steps.title: Request beta sharing
steps.when: Only to let a few users outside your Zoom account test before you publish.
instructions: Open Manage → your app → Production tab → Beta Test.
Complete the Technical Design section first.
Upload SSDLC docs, SAST and DAST results (scanner output or screenshots) and your privacy policy.
Add any 3 of: pentest summary, security policy, incident response, vuln management, dependency policy.
Under Share App, select Request to Share. Your app must support TLS 1.2+.
While shared, don't publicise the app or use Zoom's brand for it.

warnings.text: Approved URLs last 4 weeks, plus up to two 4-week extensions. Additions cap at 10 (account-level) or 100 (user-level).
Beta testers use production credentials. Point a separate Composio auth config at the Production Client ID and secret.
warnings.unconfirmed: Zoom says beta URLs live on the Production tab. We infer they use production credentials; not tested.

problems.q: The Share App section shows no authorization URL
a: Zoom only generates it once every requirement is complete. Finish Technical Design and the security uploads.
It expired after 4 weeks, or you published the app. Users already added keep working.
Select Request Extension under Share App. After publishing, use the published app instead.

steps.title: Wait for beta sharing approval
steps.when: After you select Request to Share.
instructions: Zoom's app review team answers the request. Approval is case by case.
On approval you get an email and an Approved label next to the URL.
Send the URL to testers yourself. Zoom has no way to send it.

wait.asStated: A member of the Zoom app review team responds no longer than 3-4 business days; longer if more information is needed.

steps.title: Route the callback through your domain
steps.when: Before publishing. Zoom verifies the domain of your OAuth redirect URL, and you can't verify composio.dev.
instructions: Add an endpoint on your domain that 302-redirects to the Composio callback, keeping the query string.
Set it as OAuth redirect URL and in OAuth allow lists, on Development and Production.
Set the same URI as Redirect URI in your Composio auth config.
Then verify your domain at submission: TXT record, HTML file, or meta tag.

warnings.text: Return a 302. Don't fetch Composio's callback server-side; the browser must follow the redirect.

steps.unconfirmed: Zoom offers manual domain approval via devForum (within 48 hours). We couldn't confirm it would approve composio.dev for you.

steps.title: Complete listing and technical design
instructions: Switch to the Production tab. Set OAuth redirect URL, allow lists and scopes there too.
Fill in App Listing: description, images, Privacy Policy URL, Terms of Use URL, support links.
Set a Deauthorization Notification Endpoint URL. Delete the user's data when Zoom calls it.
Complete Technical Design: architecture, security controls, and how you use each scope's data.
Expect testing against the OWASP Top 10 and a check that every scope is needed.
Unlisted is an option: still reviewed, but hidden from Marketplace search.
steps.unconfirmed: We couldn't see the Production tab, so we didn't confirm it has its own redirect URL fields. Check both tabs.

problems.q: Submission was rejected for incomplete information
a: Submission completeness checks metadata, technical design docs and security info first.
Zoom sends a remediation report. Fix every item and resubmit.

steps.title: Draft scope reasons and a test plan
instructions: Draft one Scope Description per scope, naming the agent tool that uses it.
Draft Technical Design answers: data flow through Composio, storage, encryption, retention.
Draft a step-by-step test plan for the release notes field, including how to connect Zoom.

steps.title: Submit for review
instructions: Production tab → Publish your app → App Submission.
Audience: External Zoom users. Within my account skips the standard review but stays internal.
Verify Domains: verify each listed domain.
Paste your test plan into release notes. Give reviewers a test account with placeholder data.
First submission: reviewers must authorize with the Production Client ID. Point Composio at it.
Choose activation: immediately after approval, or manually. Agree to the developer agreement and submit.

problems.q: I can't verify my redirect URL's domain
a: You can't add records to composio.dev. Use the callback proxy step, or request manual approval on devForum.

steps.title: Wait for Zoom's review
instructions: Stages: completeness and branding, functionality and compliance, then security review.
Zoom publishes no timeline. Clear scopes, a test plan and clear listing text shorten it.
Issues come back through the submission. Answer them there.

wait.asStated: No official timeline. Zoom staff on devForum: 72-hour SLA, excluding weekends and US holidays; security review can take up to 2 weeks.

problems.q: Review is taking longer than two weeks
a: Staff say the security queue alone can take up to 2 weeks, and the SLA excludes weekends and US holidays.
Ask for status in the devForum Marketplace category.

steps.title: Activate and switch to production
instructions: If you chose manual activation, select Activate on Created Apps. Until then it's Active for internal only.
Put the Production Client ID and secret in your Composio auth config.
Have test users reconnect so they authorize the production app.
steps.unconfirmed: We couldn't test whether connections made with development credentials keep working after the switch. Assume users reconnect.

steps.title: Marketplace admin pre-approves the app
steps.when: When a user's Zoom account requires app pre-approval, or your app uses :admin scopes.
instructions: The user requests pre-approval from their admin. Admins get an email from noreply@zoom.us.
The admin signs in to marketplace.zoom.us, opens your app, clicks the arrow next to Add → Manage approvals.
Or: Marketplace admin → App requests → Active requests → your app → Approve.
Admin-scope apps must be authorized by a user with matching admin role permissions.
The user then connects again from your product.
steps.unconfirmed: We didn't run the pre-approval flow, so the exact screen a blocked user sees isn't verified.

sources.title: Zoom · Sharing private and beta apps
